analysis:
The only change in this PR is one added documentation bullet in docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head line 1025, in the `darkbloom status` output list). It says App Attest serving authorization can stay visible through its unexpired lease, while MDM removal advice needs a matching fresh coordinator decision. It also says this applies to both doctor summaries and links to ../reference/provider-authorization.md. I examined both base units (lines 805-1271 and 1272-1720) and the patch excerpt. The patch does not change source code, protocol behavior, keys, attestation checks, authorization logic, cache storage or any trust boundary.

The added text is consistent with the threat model for A-016, T-053 and T-057. A-016 describes expiring coordinator authorization bound to the connection. T-057 covers premature MDM removal stranding a provider. Requiring a fresh matching coordinator decision before showing MDM removal advice reads as a conservative documentation statement. It does not weaken the control that stale authorization must not survive a connection change or revocation.

Integration questions for later passes:
- I could not verify that the linked ../reference/provider-authorization.md exists and says the same thing.
- I could not verify that the implementation in the doctor/status code matches the described behavior. No source for it was supplied.
- I identified no new attack surface and no invalidated threat assumption. No finding qualifies.
